hook: In Seoul, people often sign a two-year jun-say lease after one short viewing. What if you could live there first?
korea: Ithaca started from that problem. What you're seeing is a real run with Muse Spark one point three.
pitch: Ithaca is a pre-living agent. An AI household lives thirty days in the homes you pick, before you sign.
ask: You describe your situation in plain words. Muse reads it, and calls real tools: your profile, real homes, and the map.
candidates: The candidates come from the government's real transaction records. Each price is the median of recent jun-say deals.
live: Pick two. Muse lives thirty days in each home, with the same household and the same random seed. There's no ranking, and no winner.
days: Every trip is simulated minute by minute: real walking routes, the subway timetable, and measured crowding. Each line says whether it's measured or assumed.
results: After thirty days, you see what it costs, how long the commute really is, and what living there showed. The score follows your own criteria. It's never a verdict.
verify: Muse writes the report. Code re-checks every number, and Muse judges the evidence again. Tap any moment, and the three-D view opens at the minute it happened.
meta: Ithaca is built with Meta AI. Muse Spark one point three talks with you and makes the household's choices. Spark Open made the same choice in eighty-six percent of shared decisions. And Muse Code wrote every line of product code.
end: We walk the odyssey. You just come home.
